topics.topic: Existing witness check bound to CLK-002 Required tests
questions: Which existing check is bound to CLK-002 and is intended to assert its wall-clock and elapsed-clock obligations?

Which existing witness check is bound to the CLK-002 Required-tests item and asserts the clock-source exclusivity, reading counts, fixed-instant validity decisions, and elapsed-window behavior it names?
Which existing witness check is bound to CLK-002 and asserts its required clock-source behavior?

judgement.why: This asks the same unchanged question as P1 about the absence of an existing witness binding for CLK-002.

precedent.topic: Existing verification check bound to CLK-002 requirements
quotes: - Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: CLK-001 [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal]; CLK-001 [witness: verification:staff_bootstrap_client_portal].
precedent.why: The exhaustive witness line binds both existing checks to CLK-001 and therefore answers that no existing witness check is bound to CLK-002.

topics.topic: Required test for elapsed-clock confinement and exclusivity
questions: What test observation must show that an elapsed reading is never converted into an instant, compared or ordered with persisted timestamps, or retained outside the rate-limit window’s in-memory state?
What required test shows that no other portal path reads the elapsed clock and that viewer entry neither converts its reading into an instant nor compares it with persisted timestamps?

quotes:
- CLK-002: the clock source is the only reader of the host's wall and
  elapsed clocks; an operation takes one wall reading, and that instant
  decides every current-time comparison it makes and every portal-owned
  timestamp it writes (the audit writer's reading of `occurred_at` aside);
  the elapsed clock is read once per viewer-entry request,
  only to measure the A25 rate-limit window, and its reading is kept only
  in that window's in-memory state, never persisted, turned into an instant or ordered against a persisted record.

- CLK-002: a test that the clock source's wall reading returns the host's
  `datetime.utcnow()` and its elapsed reading the host's `time.monotonic()`,
  each read afresh on every call and returned unchanged; a test per
  operation that reads the wall clock, with the wall-clock source replaced
  by a counting source fixed at an instant years away from the host's
  time, that the operation takes exactly one reading (the audit writer one
  per appended record), that every portal-owned event timestamp it writes
  equals that instant (a TTL-derived expiry equals it plus the TTL, a
  source-supplied time stays as supplied, CLK-001), that with both host
  clocks instrumented every host-clock read during the operation is made by
  a call of the clock source, and that its validity decisions follow that instant — an expiry equal to
  it is refused, one a microsecond later accepted — so any other path to a
  host clock shows as a value that does not follow the fixed instant; and
  a viewer-entry test with a counting elapsed source that one request takes
  exactly one elapsed reading, that the window decision at its boundary
  follows that reading, and that no record the request writes holds it.
judgement.divergence: One verification implementation checks every portal path and rejects elapsed-clock use outside A25 plus conversion, ordering, or retention of its value; another checks only viewer-entry count, its boundary, and persisted records, so those violations pass, which the verification agent notices.
judgement.why: The Required test does not say what observation proves global elapsed-clock exclusivity or the prohibitions on conversion, persisted-time ordering, and retention outside the window state.

witness.initial: The clock source is instrumented, persisted viewer records contain datetime timestamps, and a valid viewer access link exists.
events: A viewer uses the access link to make a viewer-entry request.
The implementation reads the elapsed source once for A25 but also converts or compares that reading with a persisted timestamp without storing the float.
A verification agent runs the stated CLK-002 viewer-entry test.
outcomes: A comprehensive CLK-002 check rejects the implementation because the elapsed reading escaped the A25 in-memory window or was ordered against persisted time.
A check limited to one elapsed read, the rate-limit boundary, and absence of the float from written records accepts the implementation.
witness.observer: The verification agent sees rejection versus acceptance.
basis:
Without a
session the portal answers only: staff login, viewer entry with an access
link, and the liveness and readiness checks (R0-11).

the elapsed clock gives a duration scale: one reading per viewer-entry
  request of a clock that cannot move backwards, in seconds as a float, the same value
  `time.monotonic()` gives. It measures the viewer-entry rate-limit window of
  A25 only; a reading is kept only in that window's in-memory state, never
  written to a persisted record, never turned into an instant and never
  ordered against a persisted record.

topics.topic: OSV export completeness when no content length is announced
questions: If the OSV export response has no announced content length but reaches a normal end and its archive index reads successfully, does the check pass or fail as incomplete?

quotes:
every distribution installed in that image — the pins and every library
   pip resolves for them — is checked against the OSV database (osv.dev,
   ecosystem PyPI; it aggregates the PyPA advisory database), read once in
   that same deploy as one copy of the PyPI ecosystem data — OSV's
   PyPI export archive, downloaded whole: the transfer ends with the
   length the server announced and the archive's index reads without error
   (a download that is not whole is a check that cannot complete; the gate
   has no other evidence of completeness and asks for none) — against which every distribution is
   judged; no earlier verdict or advisory copy is
   reused.

A check that cannot
   complete does not pass: that deploy does not start the service, and a
   new deploy makes a new check.
judgement.divergence: One deploy gate treats normal end-of-stream plus a readable archive index as complete when no length was announced and starts the service; another treats the missing announced length as an unsatisfied completeness condition and blocks the deploy, which the release operator notices.
judgement.why: The completeness condition depends on matching an announced length but gives no outcome when the server announces no length.

witness.initial: A built image is ready and OSV serves a complete valid PyPI export without announcing a content length.
events: The deployment process downloads the export to normal completion.
The deployment process reads the archive index without error and finds no affecting non-withdrawn entry for any installed distribution.
The deployment process decides whether to start the service.
outcomes: The service starts because normal completion and a readable index suffice when no length was announced.
The service does not start because the transfer cannot equal a server-announced length when no such length exists.
witness.observer: The release operator sees the image start or remain blocked.
basis:
A deploy is the start of the service from a built image, identified by
   the immutable digest of the platform image that starts, never by a tag.

OSV's
   PyPI export archive, downloaded whole: the transfer ends with the
   length the server announced and the archive's index reads without error
   (a download that is not whole is a check that cannot complete; the gate
   has no other evidence of completeness and asks for none)

topics.topic: Required assertion for source-supplied timestamps with non-naive-UTC representations
questions: What must the test assert when a supplied timestamp carries an offset or timezone representation different from offset-naive UTC?

quotes:
Times a
source supplies — `approved_at`, `published_at` of a snapshot, `confirmed_at`
of a recognition, `photo_date`, a service credential's `expires_at` — are
kept as supplied: the same instant, stored offset-naive UTC like every
persisted timestamp, never replaced by the clock (State 1 Modeling
conventions).

a test per operation receiving
  source-supplied times (snapshot import, recognition intake, photo intake,
  service credential issuance with a supplied `expires_at`, payment
  recording) that each supplied time and calendar date is stored as
  supplied, not as the clock's instant.
judgement.divergence: One test converts an offset-bearing input to offset-naive UTC and asserts preservation of the instant; another strips the offset while preserving the displayed wall fields and still calls that value stored as supplied, which a repository-level verification agent notices.
judgement.why: The Required test does not require an offset-bearing case or explicitly assert both offset-naive UTC storage and preservation of the supplied instant.

witness.initial: The wall-clock source is fixed at 2035-01-01 00:00:00 UTC and a snapshot publication supplies `approved_at` as 2026-06-01 12:00:00+02:00.
events: A service principal imports the snapshot.
The snapshot import stores the source-supplied `approved_at`.
A verification agent reads the stored snapshot timestamp.
outcomes: The test requires and observes naive UTC 2026-06-01 10:00:00, preserving the supplied instant.
The test accepts naive 2026-06-01 12:00:00 as stored as supplied because it checks only that the wall-clock instant was not substituted.
witness.observer: The repository-level verification agent sees different stored values.
basis:
a test per operation receiving
  source-supplied times (snapshot import, recognition intake, photo intake,
  service credential issuance with a supplied `expires_at`, payment
  recording) that each supplied time and calendar date is stored as
  supplied, not as the clock's instant.

topics.topic: Required test for bootstrap audit timestamp using the operation's single instant
questions: What Required test must demonstrate that bootstrap’s audit `occurred_at` uses the bootstrap operation’s single instant rather than an audit-writer reading?

quotes:
The one exception is the `occurred_at` of an audit record appended
through the audit writer: the writer takes it when it appends (Factory
code `application/audit_writer.py` 136); the bootstrap, which builds its
own audit, keeps its one instant.

- CLK-001: all portal-owned event timestamps written by one operation, other than an
  audit record's `occurred_at`, are equal; an expiry it derives from a TTL is that instant plus its TTL, and source-supplied times, a service credential's supplied `expires_at` among them, keep their supplied values.

- CLK-001: a test per operation that writes more than one portal-owned
  event timestamp (activation, revocation cascades and bootstrap among
  them) that its portal-owned event timestamps, other than audit
  `occurred_at`, are one instant; a test per operation deriving an expiry
  from a TTL (staff and viewer session creation) that the expiry equals
  that instant plus the configured TTL; and a test per operation receiving
  source-supplied times (snapshot import, recognition intake, photo intake,
  service credential issuance with a supplied `expires_at`, payment
  recording) that each supplied time and calendar date is stored as
  supplied, not as the clock's instant.
judgement.divergence: One bootstrap test asserts that the account timestamps and its `staff.create` audit `occurred_at` all equal the bootstrap instant; another excludes the audit timestamp as the stated Required test says and accepts a later audit-writer instant, which an audit verification agent notices.
judgement.why: The bootstrap-specific normative exception requires reuse of its operation instant, but the Required test excludes every audit `occurred_at` and therefore does not say what demonstrates that exception.

witness.initial: No staff account exists, and the clock source yields T1 for the bootstrap operation and T2 for a later audit-writer read.
events: The host operator runs the first-administrator bootstrap.
The bootstrap writes the administrator account and its required `staff.create` audit record.
A verification agent compares their persisted timestamps.
outcomes: The account timestamps and audit `occurred_at` all equal T1.
The account timestamps equal T1 while audit `occurred_at` equals T2, and a test excluding audit `occurred_at` accepts the result.
witness.observer: The audit verification agent sees equal timestamps versus a later audit timestamp.
basis:
The host operator runs a local administrative command that creates exactly one active
administrator when no staff account exists, and is refused once any exists.

The first-administrator bootstrap of R0-07 is no exception: it writes one
  `staff.create` record with actor kind `system`, no actor, no project and
  the new `staff_id` as entity; the email and password it was given appear
  in no record.

topics.topic: Whether every portal operation must take exactly one wall-clock reading
questions: Must every portal operation take exactly one wall-clock reading, including an operation that writes no timestamp and makes no current-time comparison, or do only operations needing current time take one?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question as P3 about whether an operation that does not need the current instant takes no wall-clock reading.

precedent.topic: Whether operations that do not use current time may take zero clock readings
quotes:
- **Time.** Only `system_clock` reads the host clocks (A28). An operation
  that needs the current instant takes one wall reading from it and reuses
  it; the transport guard takes the elapsed reading for the viewer-entry
  window from it. No other module reads a host clock.
precedent.why: The later module rule limits the wall reading to an operation that needs the current instant, so an operation with no timestamp or current-time comparison takes none.
